- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.4) — model is overly conservative, misses upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment drops, price doesn’t fall as fast.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves — tends to overpredict decline after a spike, then overcorrects upward.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment, especially if sentiment is volatile — model reacts too aggressively to short-term sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often underestimates the continuation — fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days — focus on recent 5–7 day sentiment trend for better alignment with price direction.
